asof: Settles Thu 12 Nov 2026 · written Fri 13 Nov
headline: Iran and oil extend the selloff past the peak: M7–Z9 up 8.5–12bp, U7 at 4.835% prices almost four hikes.
summary: Cash Treasuries reopened with a bear flattener and SR3 sold off hardest from the reds out: Z7 rose 11bp to 4.81%, H8 through Z8 11.5bp and the 2029 contracts 11.5–12bp, U7 10bp to 4.835% and M7 8.5bp to 4.785%, while H7 rose 5.5bp to 4.62%, Z6 2bp to 4.315% and U6 held at 3.925%. Week-to-date U7 is 44bp higher and M7 42bp, against 17bp in Z6; from the 30 October settle M7–H8 are up 30.5–31.5bp and Z9 20.5bp. The peak is still U7 at 4.835%, 94.5bp over the 3.89% SOFR fixing, with only 23.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is close to four hikes, against three in Deutsche Bank's call (December, January, March) and two in Goldman's.
drivers: Trump drops the Iran deal and oil jumps

Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran, and attacks on Saudi energy sites plus Hormuz disruption sent Brent up $3.06 to $95.82. Inflation risk lifted the back of the strip most: H8–Z9 rose 11.5–12bp, more than U7's 10bp, while 2-year yields rose 12.1bp to 4.867%.
Hike pricing keeps building after CPI

CME FedWatch had 28.3bp for December and 65.1bp by March on Thursday, up from 27.4bp and 58.5bp. So the extra hikes went into the first quarter rather than December itself: Z6 rose only 2bp while H7/M7 widened 3bp to +16.5bp.
Hammack and Daly back more hikes, not faster ones

Cleveland's Hammack, a voter, wants a restrictive stance through smaller, more frequent moves and said the Fed is not behind the curve. San Francisco's Daly sees further tightening as likely but said higher yields give the Fed time. Neither pushed for 50bp, which kept the front anchored.
Soft long-bond auction, steady claims, Nvidia noise

The $25bn 30-year sale stopped at 5.441% with a 0.4bp tail and a 2.36 bid-to-cover, below average, but barely moved the market. Claims rose to 200k against 195k expected, and Nvidia's CEO exit hit tech stocks early without giving the reds any haven bid.
spreads: The curve steepened into the reds again and the inverted tail barely moved. U6/Z6 rose 2.25bp to +39bp and Z6/H7 3.5bp to +30.5bp (+18bp week-to-date, +9.5bp on the month), H7/M7 3bp to +16.5bp (+7bp on the week, +4bp on the month) and M7/U7 1.5bp to +5bp, while U7/Z7 rose 1bp to −2.5bp, so U7 remains the peak by 2.5bp over Z7 and 5bp over M7. Z6/Z7 widened 9bp to +49.5bp (+25.5bp week-to-date, +14.5bp on the month) and Z6/M7 6.5bp to +47bp (+25bp on the week, +13.5bp on the month). With parallel moves past the peak, Z7/H8 rose 0.5bp to −4bp, H8/M8 held at −4bp and M8/U8 and U8/Z8 at −3bp; Z7/Z8 is −14bp (−10.5bp on the week, −6.5bp on the month), Z8/Z9 −7bp (−4.5bp on the month) and U7/Z8 −16.5bp (+1.5bp on the day, −12bp on the week, −6.5bp on the month), with the 2029 consecutive spreads between −2.5bp and −1bp. The H7/M7/U7 fly rose 1.5bp to +11.5bp (+3bp on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 0.5bp to +7.5bp (+1bp on the month).
fed: The latest weekday fed funds futures snapshot, Wednesday's, prices 26.8bp for 9 December (a 93% chance of 25bp and 7% of 50bp), 43bp by January, 59.6bp by March, 74.6bp by June and a 78.5bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.665%). That compares with 27.5bp, 42.5bp, 59.1bp, 72.1bp and a 72.5bp peak on Tuesday, 20.4bp, 27bp, 41.4bp, 54.9bp and 58bp a week earlier on 4 November, and 17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp and 57bp at the 30 October month-end: December is up 9.2bp on the month and the peak 21.5bp. Thursday's FedWatch reading of 65.1bp by March shows ZQ followed SR3 higher after that snapshot. With SOFR at 3.89% and EFFR at 3.88%, Z6 at 4.315% matches the 4.31% January ZQ rate, consistent with a December hike and most of a January one, while U7 at 4.835% runs 17bp over the Wednesday ZQ peak. Deutsche Bank expects hikes in December, January and March and Goldman in December and March; Hammack and Daly favour a steady pace. At almost four hikes, the strip is above even the hawkish end of that range.

ideas.title: U7 long stopped; fade the 2027 hike path with a short Z6/M7
ideas.trade: Sell SR3Z6, buy SR3M7 (sell the Z6/M7 spread)
ideas.why: The long U7 went through its 95.20 stop as U7 rose 10bp to 4.835% (95.165), an 11bp loss from the 95.275 entry, and we close it: oil and Iran lifted the whole back of the strip, not just the peak. We still think 2027 hikes are overpriced but now express it as a spread that is protected from parallel selloffs. Z6/M7 at +47bp, up 25bp week-to-date, prices almost two more hikes after the first quarter even as Hammack and Daly argue for a steady pace. That is 8bp to target against 5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: A hot PPI or strong retail sales, or Williams backing a faster pace, could add more 2027 hikes and push the spread above +52bp.

ideas.title: Keep the U7/Z8 flattener against a longer cycle
ideas.why: Still open at −16.5bp, 1bp against us: the oil spike lifted Z8 11.5bp against 10bp in U7, so the spread rose 1.5bp on the day but is still down 12bp week-to-date. It offsets the new core: if hot data piles more hikes into 2027, U7 should lead and the spread fall, while 23.5bp of easing is still priced from U7 to Z9. That is 6.5bp to target against 2.5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: Another oil-driven selloff concentrated in the 2028 contracts would push the spread above −14bp.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 edged down 0.25bp to 3.925% and is up only 0.5bp week-to-date, while M7–Z9 rose 8.5–12bp on the day. SOFR fixed at 3.89% on 10 November with EFFR at 3.88%, and only U6's last week sees the 9 December decision, so even a 7% chance of 50bp is worth little. Refunding notes settle on 16 November with reverse repo usage near zero, so there is little cash buffer.
ideas.risk: If settlement tightens funding, SOFR could print near 3.95% and cost a couple of bp.
